attributes.residual:
UNCHANGED at real 86, insns T121/O121, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (0t), frame 248 = target, save-set r19 = target. COMPLETE r1-slot census (new this pass, both streams dumped end to end): the ONLY differing words in the whole function are the four array-base materialisations - target addi r23,r1,108 / addi r5,r1,108 and addi r25,r1,36 / addi r5,r1,36, ours the same four at 104 and 32. Every other stack word is identical (stw r0,4(r1); stwu -248; stfd f31,240; stmw r19,188; lmw 188; lwz 252; lfd 240; addi r1,r1,248). GEOMETRY: the two arrays are the function's ONLY memory-resident locals, 72 bytes (buf1, declared last, lowest) + 80 bytes (buf2) = 152. Target lays them 36..108..188, flush against the save area, with a 28-byte below-array reservation. Ours lays them 32..104..184 with a 24-byte reservation and 4 bytes of dead slack at 184..188. We are short exactly 4 bytes in the BELOW-ARRAY reservation, not in the local block.

THE PARAM-FLOOR LEVER IS REFUTED FOR THIS FUNCTION BY TARGET EVIDENCE, WITHOUT SPENDING A PROBE, AND THIS IS THE PASS'S MAIN DELIVERABLE. The law predicts the floor sits at 8 + sum(declared parameter sizes); ours is 8+16=24 for (f32,ptr,s32,s32), and target's 28 would require a 20-byte parameter list. BOTH ways of reaching 20 bytes are independently refuted: (1) A FIFTH 4-BYTE PARAMETER is impossible because BOTH call sites are already byte-EXACT with four arguments - ScrollTextWidth and StringTextWidth both measure real 0 / status EXACT in the TU gate baseline, and a fifth parameter would force an extra argument-register set-up in each, regressing two exact siblings. (2) A WIDER FLOAT PARAMETER (f32 scale -> f64, the exact move that founded the law on FindClosestWaypoint) is refuted by the target's own arithmetic: at +0x3c the target emits `fmuls f31,f1,f0`, a SINGLE-precision multiply reading the incoming f1 directly. An f64 declaration makes `scale * (f32)e->scale` a double multiply (`fmul`) plus an `frsp` for the (f32) narrowing - a different opcode and one extra instruction - and our multiset is already IDENTICAL, so either change is a strict regression. NOTE THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT FOR THE LAW: the law's stated diagnostic (frame size AGREES while a slot set is uniformly displaced => the parameter list is wrong) fires exactly here and is WRONG here. StringTextWidthSub is a confirmed counter-example: a uniform 4-byte local displacement at equal frame size can also come from the below-array reservation with a correct parameter list. The float-width half of the law needs the extra guard that an `fmuls` reading the parameter's FPR directly PROVES the parameter is f32 - the instruction stream is NOT always silent about float parameter width, contrary to the law's central claim.

THE BOTTOM-PAD AXIS IS NOW CLOSED WITH FOUR MEASUREMENTS, NOT TWO. Every attempt to add 4 bytes below the arrays lands the arrays at 36/108 EXACTLY RIGHT and then overshoots the frame by 8 (248 -> 256, save area 188 -> 196), because a dead declaration is charged twice per the nominal-area law. Prior pass: (b) u8 unused[4] innermost block, (c) s32 unused same position - byte-identical. THIS pass added two genuinely new shapes: (d) `volatile u8 unused[4]` declared after both arrays, chosen because this very TU's DrawStringTextMLines carries a `volatile u8 unused[20]` precedent and volatile forces real memory residency - REGRESSED real 86 -> 92, frame 256, save area 196, slots 196/256/260, i.e. IDENTICAL failure mode to (b)/(c); volatile does not exempt a declaration from the nominal-area charge. (e) the nominal law's predicted escape, a LIVE 4-byte function-scope scalar declared after both arrays (hoisted the existing `nlines` out of its inner block so no declaration is added or removed in net) - NEUTRAL, real 86, slots STILL 32/104. FINDING: a register-allocated live scalar contributes NOTHING to the local block, so the 'use a live declaration to dodge the double charge' escape does not exist for scalars. Four measurements, one placement mechanism, two distinct failure modes - AXIS CLOSED.

WHAT A FUTURE PASS SHOULD TRY, IN ORDER. The 4 bytes must appear in the below-array reservation WITHOUT adding a declaration. (i) Audit the OUTGOING parameter area: the reservation may be sized by the widest call's argument list read from the CALLEE PROTOTYPE rather than by this function's own parameters - FixMLineText/MBSetFont/MBSetFontScaleSpace/MBFontStringWidth are the only callees; if any real prototype is wider than ours the reservation grows with no instruction-stream change. This is the single most promising untried axis and it costs one prototype edit per callee. (ii) Look for a 4-byte COMPILER temp the target materialises and we do not (an address-taken scalar or a narrowing temp). (iii) Do NOT re-probe pad/param-width shapes.
